findings.passage: In the last days of session democrats passed SB 243 C , a deeply flawed gun control measure that does nothing to reduce gun violence, address mental health, or make our communities safer. The bill infringes on Oregonians’ Second Amendment rights by turning those who already own bump stocks and other attachments into criminals, replaces public safety with a door sign, and creates confusion across jurisdictions for concealed handgun license carriers.
findings.note: First-person end-of-session newsletter from his legislative office describing SB 243 (bump-stock/attachment limits, carry signage, Measure 114 delay) as a Second Amendment infringement. Exact date not shown on the page; session ended late June 2025.

findings.passage: An amendment that would create concealed carry reciprocity across state lines and would recognize valid Concealed Carry Licenses from other states and allow visitors to exercise their rights when coming to Oregon.
findings.note: Newsletter lists amendments his caucus offered to SB 243: repeal Measure 114, honor other states' concealed carry licenses, and allow suppressors. Presented as proposals that were rejected.

findings.passage: Thankfully, House Republicans were able to kill a different gun bill HB 3076. This bill would hurt responsible firearms dealers by adding a new state licensing program, even though arms dealers are already highly regulated by the federal government.
findings.note: Newsletter welcomes the defeat of HB 3076 (state licensing of firearms dealers), saying it would burden dealers.
